questions.question: Identify the incorrect sentence.

options.text: All of the cities in California is being affected by the rain yesterday.
Seven people were rescued from the fire.
Half of the boxes are empty.
Some of the TV programs are very interesting.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Option 1: "All of the cities in California is being affected by the rain yesterday" is incorrect because:
 
 
• The sentence uses incorrect tense and subject-verb agreement.
 
• "Is being affected" is grammatically incorrect for past events. Instead, "were affected" should be used to indicate a completed action in the past.
 
• The correct form of the sentence would be: "All of the cities in California were affected by the rain yesterday."
 
 
 
• Option 2: "Seven people were rescued from the fire" is correct. The sentence uses proper past tense and is grammatically accurate.
 
• Option 3: "Half of the boxes are empty" is correct. It uses proper plural subject-verb agreement and is grammatically accurate.
 
• Option 4: "Some of the TV programs are very interesting" is correct. It uses proper plural subject-verb agreement and is grammatically accurate.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subject-Verb Agreement:** 
 
 
• The verb must agree with the subject in both number and tense.
 
• For example: 
 
 
• Correct: "He runs every morning." (Singular subject matches singular verb)
 
• Correct: "They run every morning." (Plural subject matches plural verb)
 
 
 
 
 
• **Past Tense Usage:** 
 
 
• Past tense is used to describe actions that have already been completed.
 
• Example: "She walked to the park yesterday."
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following is free from grammatical error?

options.text: She is senior than me by two years.
He was prevented to go out by the guard.
I look forward to meet you soon.
The manager, as well as his assistants, was late.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**To identify the sentence that is free from error, let's analyze the prepositional and structural rules in each option:**

__
 
• **Option 1: She is senior than me by two years.**

 
 
• Adjectives ending in "-ior" (such as senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior) are followed by the preposition "to," not "than."
 
• The sentence is erroneous__.
 
• **The correct sentence would be:** "She is senior **to** me by two years."
 
 
 
• **Option 2: He was prevented to go out by the guard.**
 __
 
• The verb "prevented" must be followed by the preposition "from" and a gerund (verb+ing), not an infinitive ("to go").
 
• The sentence is erroneous__.
 
• **The correct sentence would be:** "He was prevented **from going** out by the guard."
 
 
 
• **Option 3: I look forward to meet you soon.**
 __
 
• In the phrase "look forward to," the word "to" is a preposition, not part of an infinitive. Therefore, it must be followed by a noun or a gerund.
 
• The sentence is erroneous__.
 
• **The correct sentence would be:** "I look forward to **meeting** you soon."
 
 
 
• **Option 4: The manager, as well as his assistants, was late.**
 __
 
• When a subject is connected by phrases like "as well as," "along with," or "together with," the verb agrees only with the **first subject**. Since "The manager" is singular, the singular verb "was" is correct.
 
• This sentence is grammatically and contextually correct__.
 
 
 
• __Therefore, out of the given options, only sentence 4 is free from grammatical error__.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate preposition:

The witness was reluctant to testify________ fear of retaliation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiomatic expression **"for fear of"** means **"because of the fear that something unpleasant might happen."**
 
• In the given sentence, the witness is reluctant to testify because he fears retaliation.
 
• Therefore, the preposition **"for"** correctly completes the sentence.
 
• The complete sentence is: *"The witness was reluctant to testify **for fear of** retaliation."*

Therefore, the correct answer is **for**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The witness was reluctant to testify **for fear of** retaliation."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **For fear of:** An idiomatic expression meaning **"to avoid something bad that one is afraid of."**
 
• **From** – Indicates source or origin and is incorrect in this context.
 
• **Of** – Cannot independently complete the sentence.
 
• **In fear of** – Although grammatically possible in some contexts, **"for fear of"** is the standard idiomatic expression used here.

questions.question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate conjunction:

_________the forecast warned of heavy rain, the outdoor ceremony proceeded as planned.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**Even though**'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The conjunction **"Even though"** is used to introduce a contrast or unexpected outcome.
 
• In this sentence, despite the warning of heavy rain, the outdoor ceremony proceeded. This indicates a contrast, making **"Even though"** the appropriate choice.
 
• **Options 2, 3**, and **4** do not fit the context because they do not convey contrast:
 
 
• **Option 2 ("Because"):** Indicates cause-effect, which is incorrect here.
 
• **Option 3 ("Unless"):** Indicates a condition, which is irrelevant to the meaning of the sentence.
 
• **Option 4 ("Since"):** Indicates cause or time, which does not align with the sentence's context of contrast.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.
 
**Complete Sentence:** *"Even though the forecast warned of heavy rain, the outdoor ceremony proceeded as planned."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: "Because"** explains a reason or cause, but the sentence requires a contrast.
 
• **Option 3: "Unless"** introduces a condition, which is irrelevant in this context.
 
• **Option 4: "Since"** indicates a reason or time, but does not fit the contrasting nature of the sentence.
</ul

questions.question:
Choose the best option to replace the underlined part to improve the given sentence. If no substitution is required, select 'No substitution.'

This paper is __made up of wood.__
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**3**' i.e. 'made from wood'.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
__
 
• The phrase **"made from"** is used when the material undergoes a transformation to create the final product.
 
• The sentence mentions "wood" as the material that has been processed to make paper, so **"made from wood"** is the correct option.
 
• **Option 1: "made of wood"** is incorrect because "made of" is used when the material is still recognizable in the final product, which is not the case here.
 
• **Option 2: "made up from wood"** is incorrect because "made up from" is not a valid phrase in standard English for this context.
 
• **Option 4: "No substitution"** is incorrect because the original sentence is not grammatically accurate.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.
 
**Correct Sentence:** *"This paper is made from wood."*
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"Made of":** Used when the material retains its form in the final product. Example: "The table is made of wood."
 
• **"Made from":** Used when the material undergoes a transformation. Example: "Wine is made from grapes."
 
• **"Made up of":** Describes the composition of something. Example: "The team is made up of skilled players."
</ul

questions.question:
- Select the sentence containing the homonym of the highlighted word:

The hunters waited patiently for the __**duck**__ to land.

options.text: The mother duck led her ducklings to the water.
The children loved to feed the ducks at the park.
He had to duck to avoid the low-hanging branch.
The artist painted a beautiful picture of a duck.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. **He had to duck to avoid the low-hanging branch.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"duck"** has two meanings in English:
 
 
• **Meaning 1:** A waterbird with a broad blunt bill, short legs, and webbed feet. (हंस/बतख)
 
• **Example:** The mother duck led her ducklings to the water.
 
• **Meaning 2:** To lower the head or body quickly to avoid something. (झुकना)
 
• **Example:** He had to duck to avoid the low-hanging branch.
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, the word **duck** is used as a verb (to lower the head or body quickly) in Option 3, which is the correct homonym for the highlighted word.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3** i.e. **He had to duck to avoid the low-hanging branch.**

---

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 1:** The mother duck led her ducklings to the water. (बतख) 
 
 
• This uses **duck** as a noun, referring to the waterbird.
 
• **Example:** The duck swam gracefully across the pond.
 
 
 
• **Option 2:** The children loved to feed the ducks at the park. (बतखें) 
 
 
• This also uses **duck** as a noun, referring to the waterbird in plural form.
 
• **Example:** Ducks often gather near lakes to be fed by visitors.
 
 
 
• **Option 4:** The artist painted a beautiful picture of a duck. (बतख) 
 
 
• This uses **duck** as a noun again, referring to the bird being painted.
 
• **Example:** The painting of the duck won first prize in the art competition.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. Harmless**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• The word **"Deleterious"** means causing harm or damage. It is often used to describe something that is harmful to health or well-being. (हानिकारक)

questions.question: Choose the option that is the most appropriate conversion of the following sentence into Direct Speech. He said that the machine operates automatically but had malfunctioned that morning.

options.text: He said, "The machine operated automatically but had malfunctioned that morning."
He said, "The machine operated automatically but had malfunctioned this morning."
He said, "The machine operates automatically, but malfunctioned this morning." morning."
He said, "The machine is operating automatically, but malfunctioned this morning."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Indirect Speech:** He said that the machine operates automatically but had malfunctioned that morning.
 
• **Key Conversions from Indirect to Direct:**
 
 
• **General Truth/Permanent State:**
 
 
• The verb **"operates"** remains in the simple present tense because it describes a general fact or a permanent characteristic of the machine. When a statement is a universal/permanent truth, the tense does not necessarily back-shift even if the reporting verb is in the past.
 
 
 
• **Tense Change (Past Perfect to Simple Past):**
 
 
• The past perfect **"had malfunctioned"** in indirect speech typically converts back to the simple past **"malfunctioned"** in direct speech to represent a completed action in the past.
 
 
 
• **Time Expression:**
 
 
• The phrase **"that morning"** is converted back to **"this morning"** in direct speech.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Structure:** The conjunction "that" is removed, and the speaker's exact words are enclosed in quotation marks, preceded by a comma.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He said, 'The machine operates automatically, but malfunctioned this morning.'"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Incorrect because it uses "operated" (changing a general fact to a past event) and fails to change "that morning" to "this morning."
 
• **Option 2:** Incorrect because it uses "operated," which would normally back-shift to "had operated" in indirect speech, unlike the original sentence.
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect because it uses the present continuous "is operating," which would change to "was operating" in indirect speech.

questions.question:
Change the following sentence into the Active form.

The students were made to write a detailed summary of the complex text.

options.text: They made the students write a detailed summary of the complex text.
The students wrote a detailed summary of the complex text.
They made the students to write a detailed summary of the complex text.
The students were made that they should write a detailed summary.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tense Identification:** The original sentence "were made" is in the **Simple Past Passive** voice.
 
• **Active Voice Rule:** To convert Simple Past Passive to Active, the structure changes from "was/were made + to + V1" to "**made + [Object] + V1 (bare infinitive)**".
 
• **Special Rule for "Make":** In the passive voice, "make" is followed by a full infinitive (**to write**). However, in the active voice, "make" is a causative verb followed by a bare infinitive (**write** without "to").
 
• **Subject Placement:** Since the passive sentence does not specify who "made" the students do the work, a placeholder subject like "They" is introduced.
 
• **Maintaining Meaning:** Option 1 correctly applies the causative verb rule and maintains the original past tense context.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"They made the students write a detailed summary of the complex text."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "The students wrote..." removes the causative element ("made"), changing the meaning from being forced to doing it voluntarily.
 
• **Option 3:** "made the students **to** write" is grammatically incorrect in the active voice; "make" requires the bare infinitive (no "to").
 
• **Option 4:** "The students were made that..." is an ungrammatical and awkward construction that does not follow standard English syntax.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect

She said, "I have completed my task."

options.text: She said that she has completed her task.
She said that she had completed her task.
She said that I had completed my task.
She said that I have completed her task.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** She said, "I have completed my task."
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Pronoun Change:**
 
 
• The first-person pronoun **"I"** changes to the third-person **"she"** because it refers to the speaker.
 
• The possessive adjective **"my"** changes to **"her"** to match the subject.
 
 
 
• **Tense Change (Present Perfect to Past Perfect):**
 
 
• Since the reporting verb is in the past tense ("said"), the present perfect **"have completed"** must be changed to the past perfect **"had completed"**.
 
 
 
• **Conjunction:**
 
 
• The conjunction **"that"** is used to connect the reporting verb with the reported speech, and the quotation marks are removed.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"She said that she had completed her task."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** Incorrect because it keeps the present perfect tense ("has completed") instead of back-shifting to the past perfect.
 
• **Option 3:** Incorrect because it fails to change the first-person pronouns ("I" and "my"), which changes the meaning of who completed the task.
 
• **Option 4:** Incorrect because it fails to change the pronoun "I" and the tense "have completed."

questions.question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

Did the renowned author finally release the highly anticipated sequel to his award-winning novel?

options.text: Was the highly anticipated sequel to his award-winning novel finally released by the renowned author?
Has the highly anticipated sequel to his award-winning novel been finally released by the renowned author?
Was the highly anticipated sequel to his award-winning novel been released by the renowned author?
Did the highly anticipated sequel to his award-winning novel be released by the renowned author?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tense Identification:** The original sentence "Did... release" is an interrogative (question) form of the **Simple Past** tense.
 
• **Passive Voice Rule:** To convert a Simple Past question into Passive Voice, the structure is: **Was/Were + Subject + V3 (Past Participle)?**
 
• **Subject-Object Swap:** The object of the active sentence ("the highly anticipated sequel...") becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• **Verb Conversion:** The auxiliary "Did" is replaced by "Was" (because "sequel" is singular), and the base verb "release" changes to its V3 form, "released."
 
• **Adverb Placement:** The adverb "finally" is placed before the main verb "released" to maintain the flow and meaning of the original sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Was the highly anticipated sequel to his award-winning novel finally released by the renowned author?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** "Has... been finally released" changes the tense to Present Perfect, which is not the tense of the original sentence.
 
• **Option 3:** "Was... been released" is grammatically incorrect because "was" and "been" cannot be used together in this manner for the Simple Past.
 
• **Option 4:** "Did... be released" is an incorrect construction; "did" is not used as an auxiliary in standard passive voice transformations.

questions.question:
Choose the correct negative interrogative form of the following sentence:

"It is essential for strong bones and teeth, and also plays a role in muscle contraction and nerve transmission."

options.text: It isn't essential for strong bones and teeth, and also plays a role in muscle contraction and nerve transmission.
It should not be essential for strong bones and teeth, and also plays a role in muscle contraction and nerve transmission.
Shouldn't it be essential for strong bones and teeth, and also plays a role in muscle contraction and nerve transmission.
Isn't it essential for strong bones and teeth, and doesn't it play a role in muscle contraction and nerve transmission?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is originally affirmative: *"It is essential for strong bones and teeth, and also plays a role in muscle contraction and nerve transmission."*
 
• To form a negative interrogative, we use **Isn't it** for the first clause and **Doesn't it** for the second clause.
 
• Options 1 and 2 are negative statements, not interrogatives, so they are incorrect.
 
• Option 3 uses **Shouldn't**, which changes the meaning of the sentence.
 
• Option 4 correctly preserves both meaning and structure, making it the right choice.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Isn't it essential for strong bones and teeth, and doesn't it play a role in muscle contraction and nerve transmission?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "It isn't essential..." – This is a statement, not a question.
 
• **Option 2:** "It should not be essential..." – Incorrect modal usage, changes meaning.
 
• **Option 3:** "Shouldn't it be essential..." – Grammatically valid but shifts the sense of necessity.
 
• **Option 4:** "Isn't it essential... and doesn't it play..." – Correct negative interrogative form, matches the original meaning.

questions.question:
Choose the correct interrogative form of the following sentence

"Copper aids in the formation of red blood cells."

options.text: Do copper aid in the formation of red blood cells?
Is copper aiding in the formation of red blood cells?
Does copper aid in the formation of red blood cells?
Has copper aided in the formation of red blood cells?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is affirmative: *"Copper aids in the formation of red blood cells."*
 
• To form an interrogative, we use the auxiliary verb **does** with singular subjects like "copper."
 
• Option 1 ("Do copper aid...") is incorrect because "copper" is singular, so "do" should be replaced with "does."
 
• Option 2 ("Is copper aiding...") changes the tense to present continuous, which alters the meaning.
 
• Option 4 ("Has copper aided...") shifts the tense to present perfect, which is not equivalent to the original sentence.
 
• Option 3 correctly preserves the tense and meaning while forming a proper interrogative.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Does copper aid in the formation of red blood cells?"*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1:** "Do copper aid..." – Incorrect subject-verb agreement.
 
• **Option 2:** "Is copper aiding..." – Changes tense to present continuous.

questions.question:
Rearrange the following sentences to form a meaningful and grammatically correct paragraph:

P. He started leaning big branches on a solid wood after discovering a natural hollow in the ground.

Q. He made a frame for the walls by weaving smaller branches between the major supports.

R. To provide insulation, he covered the structure with thick grass and leaf layers.

S. He was shielded from the rain and wind within the completed shelter.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The paragraph follows a chronological and logical sequence of building a primitive shelter, moving from foundation to completion.
 
• **Sentence P is the first sentence** as it establishes the starting point: finding a location and setting up the primary supports:
 
 
• "He started leaning big branches on a solid wood after discovering a natural hollow in the ground."
 
 
 
• **Sentence Q follows** as it describes the next logical step in construction—adding a secondary frame to the main supports:
 
 
• "He made a frame for the walls by weaving smaller branches between the major supports."
 
 
 
• **Sentence R is the third sentence** because it explains the finishing touches applied to the exterior for protection:
 
 
• "To provide insulation, he covered the structure with thick grass and leaf layers."
 
 
 
• **Sentence S is the fourth** as it describes the final result and the utility of the shelter once finished:
 
 
• "He was shielded from the rain and wind within the completed shelter."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **PQRS**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"He started leaning big branches on a solid wood after discovering a natural hollow in the ground. He made a frame for the walls by weaving smaller branches between the major supports. To provide insulation, he covered the structure with thick grass and leaf layers. He was shielded from the rain and wind within the completed shelter."

• "It was intended to lessen traffic jams and enhance the city's air quality overall."

• "The project needed a significant government investment and took more than ten years to finish."
 
 
 
• **Sentence S is the fourth** as it concludes the narrative by describing the public's reaction and acknowledging the cost mentioned in the previous sentence:
 
 
• "The system was a massive hit with commuters, even if it was expensive."
 
 
 
• The correct sequence is **PQRS**.

 

**Coherent paragraph after rearrangement**:

"A wonder of contemporary urban planning was the city's new public transport system. It was intended to lessen traffic jams and enhance the city's air quality overall. The project needed a significant government investment and took more than ten years to finish. The system was a massive hit with commuters, even if it was expensive."

questions.question: What does the word "gourmand" mean?

options.text: A person who loves and enjoys food

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. A person who loves and enjoys food**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"gourmand"** means a person who is extremely fond of eating and often eats excessively. (भोजन प्रेमी)
 
 
• **Example:** As a gourmand, she always seeks out the best restaurants in every city she visits.
 
 
• The correct word here is **"gourmand"**, which specifically refers to someone who delights in good food and often indulges in it. (भोजन का आनंद लेने वाला व्यक्ति)
 
 
• **Example:** The gourmand savored every course of the elaborate meal prepared by the chef.
 

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1 i.e. A person who loves and enjoys food**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Option 2: A person who avoids food** (भोजन से बचने वाला व्यक्ति): This refers to someone who deliberately avoids eating or has an aversion to food, which does not align with the meaning of "gourmand." 
 
 
• **Example:** A person fasting for religious reasons may avoid food entirely during specific periods.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: A type of exotic food** (एक प्रकार का विदेशी भोजन): This option refers to unique or unusual types of food that are considered rare or luxurious, but it is unrelated to the meaning of "gourmand."
 
 
• **Example:** Truffles are considered an exotic food delicacy in many cuisines.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: A type of cooking technique** (पाक कला की एक प्रकार की तकनीक): This option suggests a specific method of preparing or cooking food, which does not match the definition of "gourmand."
 
 
• **Example:** Sous-vide is a cooking technique that involves vacuum-sealing food and cooking it at a precise temperature.
